nodes.question: Is the edited counterpart of the original black DVD visibly white rather than black?
nodes.criteria: Inspect the edited endpoint, then establish which source object it corresponds to using the source image, relative scene positions, and surviving object-specific evidence. Explicitly distinguish the central printed source item and its white edited candidate from the separate object farther right. Pass if the requested source DVD has an established white counterpart; fail if its established counterpart is black or another color; unknown if source-target selection, correspondence, or color is indeterminate. Report whether a nonwhite counterpart shows intermediate or localized whitening compared with the source. A shared position supports correspondence but does not alone settle an ambiguous replacement; changed shape alone does not disprove transformation. Do not credit an unrelated white object.
nodes.binding: The black DVD specified by the instruction, identified in the source and tracked into the edit. The central printed rectangular item is a candidate locator, not a requirement to preserve a rectangular case. Do not substitute the right-hand white object merely because it looks more disc-like.

nodes.question: Does the edited counterpart of the requested source DVD remain identifiable as a DVD?
nodes.criteria: Inspect both images independently, using s1 only as advisory context. State the source target and edited counterpart being assessed. Pass if visible structure together with source identity and scene context supports that the corresponding edited object remains a DVD; fail only if evidence establishes that it has become a different kind of object; unknown if correspondence or DVD identity remains indeterminate. Specifically examine whether the central solid white oval has object structure and contextual continuity supporting DVD identity, rather than borrowing the central opening visible on the separate right-hand object. A white oval alone neither establishes DVD identity nor proves its loss. Do not demand a readable label, an unchanged case, a mandatory visible central opening, or a visually provable DVD-versus-CD distinction.
nodes.binding: The same original black DVD and its edited counterpart assessed for color, with source-to-edit matching independently verified. The central and right-hand edited white objects must not be conflated.

nodes.question: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
nodes.criteria: Compose the explicit evidence about the same original target, not the number of passes. Return complete when an established counterpart of the source DVD is white and remains identifiable as a DVD. Do not combine whiteness of one edited object with DVD identity of another. Return partial when comparison establishes requested whitening and completion is demonstrably unmet, such as an intermediate nonwhite surface or an established white transformation with loss of DVD identity. Return absent when explicit comparison evidence establishes no requested color progress on the original target; uncertain identity need not block this outcome. A failed white-endpoint check alone does not distinguish partial from absent. Unknown, skipped, or invalid observations establish neither failure nor success. If correspondence or another necessary fact leaves completion versus noncompletion genuinely uncertain, return unknown unless explicit evidence independently establishes partial or absent. Unrelated additions, target disappearance, and changed shape alone do not establish requested progress or its absence. Preserve uncertainty and do not use the reference label as evidence.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.
